hypotheses.question: Did Liquid book growth come mainly from investor share changes rather than carry profit?
hypotheses.test: Exact share-supply and conversion decomposition, holder net-flow cohorts
hypotheses.finding: 30,053 ETH growth decomposes into 19,717 share-supply effect and 10,336 share-price effect.
hypotheses.scope: Accounting identity; not actual subscription cash or isolated carry profit.

hypotheses.question: Did carry use different lenders and destinations across its history?
hypotheses.test: First/last funded events, month-end debt/position marks, migration contract lineage
hypotheses.finding: Aave WETH from June 2024, Aave USDC from August 2025, LoanManager Morpho RLUSD from June 2026; full nine material T legs visible with debt currency, HF and point rate.
hypotheses.scope: Named-account histories are bounded; current debt-token absence stays missing before deployment.

hypotheses.question: Do holder contracts obscure meaningful investor concentration?
hypotheses.test: Classify large intermediaries at T, trace receipt or gauge claims, reconcile aggregate ownership
hypotheses.finding: All 7,351 Cash accounts checked at T, 7,012 positive claims; 83 savETH and 155 gauge balances reconciled; Gearbox/Morpho and four personal HybridVault owners traced.
hypotheses.scope: Addresses are not unique people. Remote savETH CCIP ownership and other custody remain separate.

hypotheses.question: Do fee and strategy-control changes explain investor outcomes or incentives?
hypotheses.test: All captured Accountant/configuration events, receipt-confirmed payments, time-weighted fee regimes
hypotheses.finding: Nineteen successful Ethereum fee receipts match exact vault transfers; historical weETH conversions give 2,130.604903 ETH claimed.
hypotheses.scope: Ethereum platform cash, not operator profit or complete strategy income; separate OP costs/rewards.

hypotheses.question: Do current share deployment dates omit earlier product launch and migrations?
hypotheses.test: First-party launch announcements, governance proposals, deployment/first funding logs for predecessors and current shares
hypotheses.finding: Liquid issuance, Lido November 2025 predecessor and April/May 2026 crisis, earlier January YieldBasis WETH pool and later LT architecture are explicit.
hypotheses.scope: Deployment, first sampled material book and public launch are not interchanged.

hypotheses.question: What carry result can be attributed to actual financed principal after funding, rewards and fees?
hypotheses.test: Common-window claim and debt ledgers, self-credit, exact funded cohorts and complete account flows
hypotheses.finding: The 18M PYUSD cohort is -5,360 to -4,584 PYUSD after exact funding under three withdrawal conventions. The matched Lido 5M USDT lot remains +1,400.57 before gas and outer fees.
hypotheses.scope: Sensitivity models are not provenance proof, complete profits or rigorous bounds. Concrete shared/private allocation and Avant private multi-chain P&L remain unassigned.

hypotheses.question: Does the main market/carry catalogue reconcile to the product histories without changing denominators silently?
hypotheses.test: Category membership, current/historical cohort bridge, optional financing layers, no false unique total
hypotheses.finding: Thirteen product histories and canonical status census reconcile. Market adapter parents, dollar debt, receipt claims and net carry equity retain distinct denominators.
hypotheses.scope: No invented unique ETH market total or false whole-book carry concentration.

hypotheses.question: Does the reader answer BTC questions without repeated evidence/progress noise?
hypotheses.test: Visible block inventory, repeated qualifiers, product walk-through and visual comparison
hypotheses.finding: Same eight chapter route as BTC; bars and complete hovers, five deposit-to-exit stories, collapsible backing/exit proofs. Main section text is about 5,958 words versus 5,785 for BTC default view.
hypotheses.scope: Word count compares Liquid ETH with default Kraken BTC; evidence disclosures and source libraries stay available.

completion: Nonempty widgets and structural count alone do not establish substantive parity. Private data and genuinely inaccessible history must remain bounded after feasible public reconstruction.
